clue.text: Laborious painting medium included in book

indicators.note: included in says the painting medium goes inside the word for book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
oils are a medium artists paint in

explanation.surface: Oil paint tucked inside a book makes for hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laborious demands toil and effort, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Female characters in Hamlet

indicators.note: the characters or letters in the word are rearranged to form a name

explanation.surface: The women in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people in the play, but means the letters of HAMLET, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a girl's name, so it stands for a female.

clue.text: Giant tortoise, oddly, ignored openings

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A huge tortoise strangely took no notice of the gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Intros are introductions, the opening parts of songs or talks.

clue.text: Sennacherib's land as free country

indicators.note: free of means without, so the word as is taken away

parts.note: Sennacherib was a king of ancient Assyria
as taken as written

explanation.surface: The Assyrian king's realm as a liberated nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like an adjective for the country but signals removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Name change for Ron and Mike

indicators.note: change signals that the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ron and Mike decide to rename themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges RON and MIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A moniker is an informal word for a name or nickname.

clue.text: A poet's tiptop wine

parts.note: John Clare was an English poet of the 19th century
read as tip-top, the top letter of the word tip

explanation.surface: A poet praises a first-class wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiptop' looks like praise of the wine but splits as the top of 'tip', its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, a kind of wine.

clue.text: Pirate's underwear

definitions.meaning: Long John Silver is the pirate of Treasure Island, so this is his possessive

explanation.definitionFit: The possessive of Stevenson's pirate's name reads the same as the term for long thermal underpants.

clue.text: Mocking bird with lyre shaped tail

parts.note: a rail is a wading bird

indicators.note: shaped says the letters are reformed into another order

explanation.surface: A bird that mimics, with a tail shaped like a lyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mocking bird' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Mocking' is the definition. 'shaped' is the anagram signal, and 'tail' places its result at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing, so mocking talk.

clue.text: Boche fighter's right to counter bosh

parts.note: Tommy was the nickname of the British soldier who fought the Germans

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the word is turned round

explanation.surface: A British soldier's right to answer German nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boche' is old slang for Germans. 'counter' reverses TO to give OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot and bosh are both old-fashioned words for nonsense.

clue.text: Regent in play coming on to the stage

indicators.note: play means the letters are put loosely into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A ruling regent appears in a theatre production as he walks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is the anagram signal, rearranging REGENTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor entering is one walking onto the stage.

clue.text: Feeble at home, requiring company

parts.note: in means at home
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Someone frail and housebound needs others around.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirm person is weak through age or illness, so feeble.

clue.text: Regretful miss taking part in hypnotism

indicators.note: taking part in means the answer is a portion of the following word

explanation.surface: A sorry young woman joins a hypnosis session.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Otis Regrets is a Cole Porter song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cole Porter song title makes this lady the one who regrets.

clue.text: Jock and a mate dressed in revolutionary garb

indicators.note: dressed suggests the letters are arranged or prepared into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scotsman and his friend wear clothes of the revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' is the anagram signal on JOCK and A MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The high-collared tunic associated with Chairman Mao was the garment of China's communist revolution.

clue.text: Very merry

definitions.meaning: ... is British informal for very, as in ... good

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an informal intensifier and a word for cheerful.

clue.text: Addict from America getting series on TV

parts.note: US is short for the United States
ER was a long-running American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: An American drug addict hooked on a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a drug addict.

clue.text: Pathetic drip means to become a superhero

indicators.note: pathetic suggests a feeble, disordered state, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A feeble wimp has the means to turn into a superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pathetic' rearranges DRIPMEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is a Marvel comic superhero.

clue.text: Movement of small popular singer around Australia

parts.note: Cher is a famous pop singer

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for Australia back to front

parts.note: Oz is informal for Australia

explanation.surface: A minor pop star tours Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests motion or a political cause, but here it is a section of a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively section of a symphony or sonata, a musical movement.

clue.text: Influential group, as in a mountainous region

indicators.note: in places the small word inside the word for the group

parts.note: a caucus is a powerful faction within a party

explanation.surface: A powerful faction, as in a highland area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caucasus is a mountain range and region between the Black and Caspian Seas.

clue.text: A whimsical setting for Turner's first etching

indicators.note: setting for means acting as a frame round the next piece

parts.note: quaint means oddly old-fashioned or whimsical

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Turner

explanation.surface: An odd frame for an early work by the painter Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' suggests a picture frame, but it puts QUAINT round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatint is an etching technique producing tonal effects like watercolour.

clue.text: Get a hundred and twenty-four sheets

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a quire is a measure of 24 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Buying a hundred and twenty-four sheets of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a traditional stationer's measure of 24 (sometimes 25) sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to obtain or get it.

clue.text: Test for Northumberland town without aspirations

indicators.note: an aspirate is the breathy letter, so dropping aspirations removes those letters

parts.note: Hexham is a market town in Northumberland, northern England

explanation.surface: An examination for a town in the north that lacks ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspirations' looks like ambitions but means H sounds, both dropped from HEXHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a test of knowledge.

clue.text: A vessel in the Java Sea

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A ship sailing on the Java Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container for flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A vase is a container, and a vessel is any hollow container.

clue.text: Observe members being long-winded

indicators.note: the members or parts of the word are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Watch politicians droning on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' rearranges the letters of OBSERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbose writing or speech uses too many words, so it is wordy.

clue.text: Polish — not middle Euro pean

indicators.note: not middle drops the central letter of the word

parts.note: a Finnish person is a European, the printed split is a typesetting break

explanation.surface: Polish, not a central European nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality, but it means a final coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish a surface is to polish it.

clue.text: My clue could be "Ballroom where Aristotle taught"

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A setter boasts about a clue describing a dance hall and an ancient school.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: 'could be' rearranges MY CLUE. The definition joins the London dance venue and the Athenian school of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyceum was both a famous London dance hall and the grove in Athens where Aristotle lectured.

clue.text: Notorious brothers, we hear, in fashion

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: the Kray twins were notorious London gangsters of the 1960s

explanation.surface: The infamous gangland brothers were stylish dressers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie and Reggie Kray were East London gangsters, and their surname sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a passing fad or vogue.

clue.text: Impractical sylph?

definitions.meaning: a sylph is a spirit of the air, so whimsically an aerial sprite

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means vague and unrealistic, while a sylph is literally an elemental spirit of the air.

clue.text: Iron rim designed by physicist

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: designed means the letters are planned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An iron wheel rim created by a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Fermi was an Italian-American nuclear physicist.

clue.text: Mark letter from Greece about Trojan leader

indicators.note: about says the Greek letter goes round the other piece

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of Trojan

explanation.surface: A Greek letter about the head of the Trojans leaves a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, or a visible mark or spot.

clue.text: Learning about downfall of part of France

indicators.note: about says the word for learning wraps round the other piece

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning
rain is a downfall from the sky

explanation.surface: Scholarship is concerned with a French region's decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' suggests ruin, but it is literally what falls down: rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorraine is a historic region in north-eastern France.

clue.text: Pocketing money, a relative protests

indicators.note: pocketing says one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative
tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A family member pockets cash during demonstrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ins are protests where demonstrators occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: London borough or Hebridean island's leading actor

indicators.note: leading puts the island ahead of the actor

parts.note: Lewis is the northern part of the largest island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: Choosing between a London district and the star of a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewisham is a borough in south-east London.
